_doc_walkSceneKey: the town's EXPLORABLE scene key — stated role, not inferred (district fixed-camera bundles carry the whole town's collision, so pad names cannot identify the walk scene). This is the real-time DEVELOPER view; the game routes players into playSceneKey.
_doc_playSceneKey: the scene the GAME sends players to — the town played as a sequence of FIXED pre-rendered shots (the FF grammar this project exists for). Deliberately separate from walkSceneKey: the real-time bundle stays as the developer's explore view, and which of the two the scene graph wires is a data choice, not a naming coincidence.
_doc_cameraFile: the authored shot list, and which walk records each shot OWNS. tools/cine_solve.mjs solves it into townmap/dellhollow.cameras.solved.json, tools/scenegraph_derive.mjs derives the silent camera-cut edges from that, tools/cine_bake.py bakes the art. Adding or re-aiming a camera is an edit THERE, never here.
_doc_landmark_footprint: `footprint` on a class-'area' landmark: a LIST of axis-aligned rectangles [x0,x1,y0,y1] in MAP coordinates. Their union IS the pad; `extent` stays the fallback for any landmark that has no footprint, and nothing else about the landmark changes.

RULED by the coordinator 2026-08-01 after walk_water_audit found the town's four worst walk-on-water records were the four `area` pads: the derive turns `extent` into a filled disc, and at the waterfront that disc is parked on the river.
A LIST rather than one rectangle because these landings are L-shaped - fish-dock keeps 18.7 m2 of real deck as two rects against 10.4 as one, north-landing 20.4 against 12.0.

EVERY RECT MUST BE MEASURED-LANDED, and tools/landing_footprint.py's all-landed rule IS the definition: on a 0.2 m grid, from just under the pad's top surface, the first RENDER-VISIBLE hit must be a solid within 0.60 m of the foot (walk_water_audit's own rule, so the two instruments cannot disagree). A rectangle that has not been measured that way is not a legal footprint.

NOT THE SAME FIELD AS EMBERBROOK'S: emberbrook.map.json's watermill carries `footprint` as [W,D,wallHeight], a STRUCTURE BODY read by emb_blockout. The two are told apart by shape - a list of 4-number rects here, a 3-number vector there - and a derive that reads one must never be handed the other.
premise: A lock-town: the river descends the gorge in a staircase of locks, and the town exists to pass boats down them. Its vertical architecture mirrors the river's own descent.
units: world units (1u ~ 1m). Axes: x = along-gorge (downstream/north positive), y = cliff face (0) toward river (~30), z = height (water ~0).

mapDiscovery.rule: Entering a parcel's scene reveals that parcel region and its mapVisible landmarks on the player map (Vesper is a mapmaker — the map inks itself in as she walks it). Landmarks with mapVisible:false are never auto-revealed; they appear only via in-person discovery or story events.

exits._redline_2026-08-02b: MOVED 2026-08-02 under USER REDLINE #4 (see the note on the 'valley-road' landmark): 'I thought that the exit marker should be right at the bottom of this screenshot ... so right at the bottom edge.' `at` goes 'valley-gate' -> 'valley-road'. It proves the exit stood where the SPAWN stood; the user was telling us that BOTH were in the wrong place, because they read this ground as a road and a road's exit belongs at its mouth. scenegraph_derive puts the trigger on the landmark and backs the arrival off along the first street edge toward the gate (2.2 + 1.1 = 3.3 m), so the player now materialises ON the road facing up it and leaves by walking down it.
exits._redline_2026-08-02: SUPERSEDED BY _redline_2026-08-02b ABOVE — kept because the measurements in it are still true and the reasoning is the trap. USER REDLINE #1 (live play): 'I can't find any exit point from the main entrance gate to exit back to the overworld — I just found it placed very confusingly NOT at the entrance where I first spawned.' HELD, NOT MOVED, and here is the history that says why. This exit has sat at 'valley-gate' since the map was founded (bdec2ac); `git log -S valley-gate-out` finds exactly one commit, so it was never moved for a seam reason or any other. MEASURED against the shipped scenegraph: the exit trigger stands ON the gate at runtime [16.67, 24.04, -4] and the arrival from the overworld spawns at [13.58, 24.07, -5.16] — 3.30 m away, one step outside its own 2.2 m radius, which is the spawn-backoff rule working. THE EXIT WAS ALREADY AT THE SPAWN. What was wrong is that the player could not GET BACK to either: the gate tier's only walkable connection to the rest of the town is the 'stairs valley-gate->inn' flight, and USER REDLINE #2 reports that flight is unclimbable. An exit you cannot reach reads exactly like an exit in the wrong place. The fix is REDLINE #2's passage, not a move — moving this exit down to the shelf street would have put the way out of town somewhere that is not the gate, which is what the redline asks us NOT to do.

landmarks.name: Moorage
landmarks.note: the tar-dark boat waits here | FOOTPRINT STAMPED 2026-08-01 (coordinator ruling, stilt waterfront footprints): the extent-4 disc put 64 m2 of walkable pad on the river and walk_water_audit measured 607 samples of it standing on open water — the town's worst walk-on-water record. tools/landing_footprint.py finds NO all-landed rectangle of 1.5 m2 anywhere inside the disc; 3% of it is landed. The two rects stamped here are the moorage's REAL built landing, measured on lf_stage_moorage (largest all-landed rect 6.8 x 1.8) and lf_stage_moorage_w (1.0 x 3.0), both built by locksfoot_build.py and both largely OUTSIDE the old disc — which is exactly what that file's own comment says: 'everything the moorage WORKS with has to stand off it'. THE ONE PLACE NEW DECK IS OWED: the ruling asks for a modest pier under whatever of the staging still stands over water. | THE PIER IS BUILT 2026-08-01, and the third rect is it. Measured reason: with only the two staging rects the pad was an ISLAND — a connected-component sweep over walk_bodygate's own step rule put 3474 of its lattice nodes in a component containing nothing but itself, because town_blockout draws every incident ribbon to `pos` (76.09, 27) and `pos` is 4.3 m short of the staging. tools/waterfront_landings.py builds the connecting pier (7.6 m2 of planking on 2 joists and 4 piles, deck top 1.044, material and height both read off lf_stage_moorage so it continues that deck rather than inventing one) and this rect is measured all-landed over it. WIDTH 1.80 m, not the 2.00 m the landing rule asks for: walk_e_moorage__lock-five_l0 slopes down to 0.67 across the pier's east 0.14 m, and honouring it at full width would have put the deck 0.595 m under the pad — inside the 0.60 m rule by 5 mm, which the planking's own jitter would have spent. | THE WEST LINK IS BUILT 2026-08-05, and the FOURTH rect is it. The 2026-08-01 pier joined the staging to `pos`; it did not join the WEST STORE rect [70.9,71.9,26.2,29.2] to anything, because waterfront_landings' connective rect runs 2.0 m about `pos` and the west store is not in that column — so the one rect that ruling had already found to be an island stayed one, and it is a ONE-WAY PIT: walk_pad_tenant-shack (1.92..2.04) hangs 0.72 m over its 1.199 deck, which is a legal 0.79 m step DOWN and 0.16 m past STEP_UP coming back, with the pad's own slab 20 mm inside the body's blocking window over that floor ([1.85, 2.50]). The Chapter Two playtest agent stepped down at step 75 of run-20260805-054441 and was still on it at step 120 — 46 of 120 steps, filing five reports about pillars. tools/moorage_westlink.py measures the gap (2.46 m of open water; both banks lf_planking at top 1.199; the body window 1.85..2.50 CLEAR) and plank-links it; these FOUR rects are measured 228/228 all-landed over that deck. THE SHAPE IS THE MEASUREMENT: a 0.15 m occupancy scan of the body window (1.85..2.50 over a 1.199 floor) finds exactly two obstructions and they are at OPPOSITE CORNERS — the stair's t03/t04 undersides fill x 74.30..75.50 for y <= 28.50 (north-EAST), and lf_railings, the west store's own guard, fills a diagonal x 71.00..71.45 for y 28.95..29.55 (south-WEST). Of the six l2 treads only those two have an underside in that window at all: t02's is 2.55 (clears by 50 mm) and t05's TOP is 1.66 (under it). The only single rectangle that misses both corners is 0.15 m wide, which is why this is three overlapping rects and not one.

landmarks.name: Keepers' Cottage
landmarks._steps_retired_2026-08-05: THE PORCH STEPS DOWN TO THE BASIN ARE SCENERY NOW, and the walk records are gone (coordinator ruling). The `stairs keepers-cottage->lock-five` edge carried 2.63 m of rise over 3.13 m of run on its first leg — 40 degrees, the steepest flight in the town — and at that grade the tread TWO ABOVE you sits 0.75 m up, inside blocked()'s [+0.65, +1.30] body window, so every tread was roofed along the flight's own line (measured: standing at [94.11, -23.85] on floor 6.02, SIM.blocked names walk_e_keepers-cottage__lock-five_l0_t03). Three fixes were BUILT and measured and none cured it: the v2 pivot split (turns are 94/25/27 deg, the offset ramp barely engages), a per-edge riser cap (0.28 -> drive 8/25 to 10/34: a smaller riser buys vertical clearance and spends horizontal), and a full REGRADE to 25 degrees (landings 48/54/55%% -> 93/84/92%%, but the split's own 2.40 m displacement put two legs over the lock basin — the river's near bank is y~26 — and every waypoint set that stays dry falls back to 14/24 because the rungs then sit closer than a tread is wide). 4 m of y between this porch and the bank cannot hold both. A STAIR THAT CANNOT BE WALKED MUST NOT CARRY WALK RECORDS: it was a trap the metre-Dijkstra preferred, and run-20260805-014451 had already walked ch2.dock -> winches -> END CARD in six steps without it. The way down is cottage -> weave bridge -> the moorage flight, which is the route the 2026-08-05 receipt run actually walked. THE ART STAYS (lg_ks_* in the master) and is now UNREPRODUCIBLE BY ITS OWN BUILDER: lg_build.py derives it from `walk_e_keepers-cottage__lock-five_*`, which no longer exist, so re-running lg_build DELETES the visible stair. If that flight ever needs rebuilding, restore this edge first.

landmarks._redline_2026-08-02:
USER REDLINE #4, 2026-08-02 — THE GATE SCENE IS A ROAD, NOT A PLACE. This supersedes both the 'THE YARD IS NOT THE PROBLEM AND MUST NOT BE CUT' ruling (DAYLOG 2026-08-02) and the 'HELD, NOT MOVED' resolution of USER REDLINE #1, and it explains why neither of them landed.
VERBATIM: 'what you are currently calling the porter's yard is not meant to be an occupied space, and I thought this is just literally where the character should walk in. This is supposed to be the path where the character walks into the village and enters the village from... I thought that the exit marker should be right at the bottom of this screenshot... so right at the bottom edge. The path should extend past that bottom edge, and it should clearly look like a path. I think we should not be having any sort of porter's yard or anything like that at this entry scene. It should literally just be the path that leads the player into the gate of the town.'
THE MISUNDERSTANDING, stated so it is not repeated: the map modelled this ground as an AREA landmark (a yard, class 'area', extent 4, with a resident) and every downstream rule then protected it as a PLACE — the walk floor filled it, the clearance tests defended it, and the 'is it used?' test passed because 64 m2 of empty paving is walkable. The user has only ever read it as a ROAD. That is why: (a) they called it 'completely empty' while the measurements called it 'used'; (b) their chop line looked like it contradicted a standing ruling when it never did; (c) REDLINE #1's exit felt 'very confusingly NOT at the entrance' — an exit anchored to the 'valley-gate' LANDMARK sits at the gate, but a road's exit belongs at the ROAD'S MOUTH, off the bottom of the gate plate.
CORROBORATION, measured 2026-08-02: 'porter-chief', the yard's only listed resident, IS AUTHORED NOWHERE — not in npcs.json, not in any dialogue. The yard has never had anything on it, so nothing is lost by deleting it.
WHAT THIS ASKS FOR: (1) DELETE the porters-yard landmark and its walk pad; there is no yard at the entry scene. (2) The ground becomes a PATH — road-width, directional, legibly a road surface rather than a plaza, running from the gate down toward the camera. (3) The path RUNS OFF THE BOTTOM EDGE of the gate frame, so it reads as continuing to the overworld rather than stopping at a rim. (4) MOVE the overworld exit 'valley-gate-out' to the path's mouth near that bottom edge, and move the arrival spawn with it, so the player enters walking UP the road and leaves by walking DOWN it. (5) The blue-line chop of REDLINE #3 is SUBSUMED by this: narrowing to a road is the chop, done for the right reason.

_doc_passages: A PASSAGE is a PROMPTED transition between two places inside this town, for a connection the player is meant to make and cannot walk. It is not a walk edge and must never become one: `edges` means walkable ground, and every consumer treats it that way (cine_regions looks for its ribbon, routes_derive walks it, the blockout builds a flight for it). A passage carries no ground.

tools/scenegraph_derive.mjs turns each one into a reciprocal pair of scene-internal edges (to === from, `cam` filled in, a prompt on `defaults.key`) — the same record the camera cuts already use, with a label instead of `auto`. play3d.html switches on nothing new.

AN END IS EITHER A LANDMARK (`"at": "<id>"`, taking its walk pad, exactly as a door does) OR A STATED POINT (`"pos": [x, y, h]` in MAP coordinates, for a place with no landmark). A stated point's HEIGHT and its OWNING SHOT are still measured — walk surface, ownership regions — never declared.
_passages_deleted_2026-08-06: The 'gate-stair' passage (foot [22,5.5,19] <-> head [20.5,6.2,24], USER REDLINE #2's stopgap while the S-bend was unclimbable) is DELETED under the user's Bet 2 ruling: two ways down to the shelf confused; the descent is now ONE wide straight walkable flight (see edge valley-gate->inn, _superseded_S_bend_2026-08-06) and a teleport prompt beside a working stair is the second way down.
